subject: Art & Design
title: The Eiffel Tower: From Eyesore to Icon
description: Learn The Eiffel Tower: From Eyesore to Icon in one minute.

hook.text: When the Eiffel Tower was built in 1889, Paris intellectuals signed a petition calling it a 'metal asparagus.'

buildup.text: Gustave Eiffel's iron lattice tower was meant to be temporary — built for the 1889 World's Fair, then dismantled.

discovery.text: It was saved because of its radio antenna. Practical utility rescued an architectural experiment from demolition.

twist.text: It was the world's tallest structure for 41 years. Today it's the most-visited paid monument on Earth.

climax.text: The tower is repainted every 7 years with 60 tons of paint. Three shades: darkest at the bottom, lightest at the top.

punchline.text: Yesterday's eyesore is today's global icon. Taste evolves.

quiz.question: Why was the Eiffel Tower not demolished after the 1889 World's Fair?
options: Its radio antenna made it practically useful
The demolition would have been too expensive

details.summary: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 Paris World's Fair as a temporary structure. Leading artists and intellectuals signed a petition calling it a metal asparagus and a tragic lamppost. Today it is the world's most visited paid monument, attracting 7 million visitors annually.
details.whyItMatters: The Eiffel Tower's journey from public outrage to beloved icon shows how architectural taste changes. What one generation condemns, the next celebrates — a lesson for every controversial building project today.
takeaways: Built for the 1889 World's Fair as a temporary structure
Leading artists initially condemned it as an eyesore
Now the world's most visited paid monument

faq.question: Why was the Eiffel Tower originally hated?
faq.answer: Prominent artists including Guy de Maupassant and Alexandre Dumas fils signed a protest calling it a disgrace to Paris. They considered iron an industrial material unworthy of the city's stone-built elegance.

faq.question: Why wasn't the Eiffel Tower demolished after the fair?
faq.answer: Eiffel saved it by demonstrating its value as a radio antenna. By 1910 it transmitted radio signals across France. During World War I it intercepted enemy communications. Its scientific usefulness secured its survival, and by then Parisians had grown to love it.
